1994.organization: Boys & Girls Clubs of St. Lucie County
1994.description: BGCSLC’s Lincoln Park Clubhouse creates a safe location in this community for youth development. It features a 21,550 square foot one-story building with multi-functional classrooms; a computer room; a library; a commercial kitchen; areas for indoor/outdoor recreation (putt-putt golf, basketball, and pickleball); a garden, and space for community meetings and events hosted by BGCSLC, other local agencies, and St. Lucie Public Schools (SLPS). Functioning as both a Clubhouse and a community hub, BGCSLC will serve up to 800 youth, predominantly middle and high school students, with opportunities for their families and younger children to participate in activities at this location.
1994.purpose: Construction of the Lincoln Park Clubhouse would facilitate access to a safe neighborhood location for youth for BGCSLC to deliver a full complement of educational, recreational, and social programs and services to an estimated 800 youth and their families in this area. BGCSLC’s mission is to enable all young people, especially those who need us most, to reach their full potential as productive, caring, responsible citizens.
1994.activities: This Clubhouse will offer a year-round safe space for youth to advance academically; build workforce readiness and life skills; explore careers; intern locally; develop leadership skills; enjoy recreation and discover healthier lifestyles; explore cultural interests; socialize and receive encouragement and mentoring from the BGCSLC community. Youth are provided nutritious snacks and meals daily.
1994.direct_services: Clubhouse will be used as a hub to host family and community events; offer outreach by local agencies, non-profits, and the school district; and cultivate company youth internships. Economic impact demonstrates public sector cost savings and avoidance through lower grade retention rates, higher promotion and graduation rates, lower dropout rates, and lower juvenile justice referral/intake rates.
1994.population: The target population served by this project includes K-12 youth, including at-risk and disadvantaged individuals, and, by extension, their families. Some programming at the Lincoln Park Clubhouse will specifically concentrate on workforce readiness skills for middle and high school youth. The Clubhouse will serve up to 800 youth.
1994.outcome: Expected outcomes of BGCSLC’s evidence-based programming include: 1) improved educational outcomes; 2) on- target high school graduation; 3) acquisition of workforce skills and/or pre-apprenticeship training; 4) employment and/or internships; 5) reduced gang activity; 6) reduced substance abuse; 7) learned/improved positive decision- making; 8) improved physical and mental health; and 9) increased cost savings/cost avoidance and return on investment. Outcomes are measured through quantitative and qualitative methods: 1) Youth and parent/guardian surveys; 2) Annual assessment through the Boys & Girls Clubs of America's National Youth Outcome Initiative to measure attitudes and behaviors; 3) O

1719.description: Pasco County (County) requests funding to upgrade our current decontamination capabilities by placing a new, advanced Fire Rescue Decontamination Truck into service. Designed to operate at fire scenes where firefighters are exposed to IDLH (Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health) environments, this upgraded unit will provide immediate gear exchange, on scene cleaning of SCBA and PPE, and gross decontamination. These enhancements will significantly reduce exposure to cancer-causing carcinogens and other hazardous contaminants. By modernizing our equipment and response protocols, this project represents a critical investment in the long-term health, safety, and operational readiness of our firefighters
1719.purpose: These funds will be used to upgrade the County's decontamination capabilities by replacing our current Decon Truck with a more advanced and specialized unit. This upgraded truck will enhance on-scene gear exchange and gross decontamination procedures, significantly reducing firefighter exposure to harmful carcinogens. It represents a vital step forward in protecting the health and safety of our personnel during IDLH (Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health) incidents.
1719.activities: To meet the intended purpose of these funds, the upgraded Fire Rescue Decontamination Truck will deliver several key activities and services focused on firefighter health and safety. These include on-scene gear exchange to immediately replace contaminated personal protective equipment (PPE) with clean gear, reducing exposure to carcinogens. The truck will also provide gross decontamination services using specialized equipment to remove toxic substances from gear and skin before firefighters retu
1719.direct_services: This project will provide direct services to citizens by enhancing firefighter safety and operational readiness, resulting in more effective emergency response. The upgraded Decontamination Truck will reduce the risk of secondary contamination in public areas by performing on-scene decontamination of gear and personnel exposed to IDLH areas. By protecting firefighter health, the project ensures a
1719.population: The target population served by this project includes the approximately 634,000 residents and visitors of Pasco County who rely on fire rescue services for emergency response and public safety. By enhancing firefighter health and operational readiness, the upgraded Decontamination Truck will indirectly benefit the entire community through safer, more effective service delivery.
1719.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is improved long-term health and safety for Pasco County firefighters through reduced exposure to hazardous substances encountered during emergency responses. This benefit will be measured by tracking the frequency of Decon Truck deployments to high-risk incidents and monitoring trends in firefighter health and wellness over time.

1055.description: Adults living with severe and persistent mental illness (SPMI) lack the vocational skills needed to succeed in today's workforce. Nationwide, the unemployment rate for adults living with serious mental illness averages 85-90%. Skills training and job placement are the key components to helping adults living with mental illness to reintegrate into society and become economically self-sufficient. Foot Print to Success, based in Broward County, is an accredited program of Clubhouse International and partners with local businesses to offer adults with severe and persistent mental illness (SPMI) the opportunity to reenter the workforce, engage in competitive employment and become productive, tax-paying citizens. A new 12-week culinary program will offer hands-on culinary instruction, ServSafe certification, café and barista experience, virtual and Saturday classes, transportation, and employe
1055.purpose: Foot Print to Success recently opened a teaching culinary kitchen to train adults with Serious and Persistent Mental Illness (SPMI) for jobs in the restaurant and hospitality industries. State funding will support 4 cohorts of a 12-week program, reaching up to 100 adults, offering culinary, management, and barista training with virtual and Saturday classes increasing accessibility for members. This training builds skills and confidence for independence and long-term employment.
1055.activities: State funds will support vocational and culinary training, job readiness, and supported employment for adults with Serious and Persistent Mental Illness (SPMI). Activities include hands-on culinary instruction, networking, internships, mentorships, job coaching, job placement, virtual and Saturday classes, and employer outreach for successful workforce integration.
1055.direct_services: The funding will provide adults with SPMI hands-on culinary and vocational training, ServSafe certification, job readiness instruction, and supported employment. Services include interview coaching, skill building, workshops, transportation to worksites, café and barista experience, and employer outreach to place members in jobs and ensure on-the-job success.
1055.population: 200 adult citizens identified as chronically unemployed, economically-disadvantaged and diagnosed with severe and persistent mental illnesses living in Broward County.
1055.outcome: The project will equip adults with Severe and Persistent Mental Illness (SPMI) with vocational, culinary, and job readiness skills, leading to stable employment, increased economic self-sufficiency, and reintegration into the workforce and community. Participants will gain confidence, independence, and improved mental health through meaningful work and supportive peer and staff engagement. Outcomes will be measured by completion of the 12-week training program, acquisition of industry certifications such as ServSafe, placement in transitional or supported employment, job retention, and ongoing employment stability. Additional metrics include participant wages earned and engagement with emplo

2939.description: For the past 50 years, NEFBA has offered a quality, registered-apprenticeship program to provide career development in the skilled trades as a pathway to high-wage, high-demand careers in the construction industry. Employers, who sponsor apprentices through our Program, pay the apprentice's tuition over the course of the four years and the apprentices complete with zero debt and are averaging salaries of $62,000 per year. Funding from this project will support operational expenses for the new NEFBA Workforce Education Center. This center is essential to meeting the growing regional demand for a highly skilled workforce, exemplified by a 12% increase in apprentices since our last appropriation request. Currently, we serve 542 apprentices across four trades, with plans to expand capacity to 600 apprentices by 2028.

1729.description: This project funds the full construction and refurbishment of five aging lift stations: LS-03, 34, 47, 49, and 67. The comprehensive rehabilitation will address structural, mechanical, and electrical system deficiencies to restore the stations to a like-new condition. This critical work will ensure the reliable operation of essential wastewater infrastructure and prevent sanitary sewer overflows to protect public health and the environment.
1729.purpose: The purpose is the critical and timely refurbishment of five lift stations that are nearing the end of their operational life. These funds will be used to construct and refurbish these stations to prevent catastrophic failures that would cause sanitary sewer overflows, thereby protecting public health and safeguarding the significant state and local investment in our coastal water quality and world-renowned beaches.
1729.activities: Funds will be used to cover the cost of construction to improve the lift stations.
1729.direct_services: An improved sewer system that will be more efficient and reliable.
1729.population: "This project will directly protect the health and property of over 117,000 Clearwater residents connected to our sanitary sewer system. By preventing system failures, it also safeguards our vital tourism population and the businesses that depend on clean beaches and waterways
1729.outcome: We expect an improvement in lift stations being rehabilitated in safety, efficiency, and capacity. We will continue to monitor these lift stations after construction is complete and expect to see less problems from these lift stations in maintenance or more serious failures such as sewer overflows.

1149.description: The Elder Meals for Seniors Program supports elderly residents of Miami-Dade County by providing home-delivered meals to those who are homebound and congregate meals at senior centers. Transportation is included for center participants, with drivers assisting passengers and ensuring safety, especially for those in wheelchairs. The program also works to reduce social isolation and improve nutritional health through annual assessments, while preventing duplication of services from other providers. Additionally, respite care is offered to caregivers of frail, homebound older adults, giving them time to rest or attend to personal needs. The program will serve 21,020 congregate meals, 622 emergency congregate meals, 13,195 home delivered meals, 316 home delivered emergency meals. Caregivers will receive a total of 7,822 hours of service. An estimated 260 unduplicated clients will be served.

1739.description: The bluff is quickly eroding away into the inter-coastal at 3.5 feet per year. This project will specifically restore and preserve the bluff, preventing any damage to the surrounding homes and roadway. This is a prideful point for Belleair, as this bluff is one of two naturally occurring bluffs in the state of Florida. As soon as the design and engineering are complete for the bluffs project, staff will immediately engage in construction.
1739.purpose: The bluff is quickly eroding away into the inter-coastal at 3.5 feet per year. This project will specifically restore and preserve the bluff, preventing any damage to the sourrounding homes and roadway. This is a prideful point for Belleair, as this bluff is one of two naturally occurring bluffs in the state of Florida. As soon as the design and engineering are complete for the bluffs project, staff will immediately engage in construction.
1739.activities: A restored and maintained bluff will attract more residents and tourists who will use it for such recreation as walking, running and yoga. The applicant will frequently count the number of people using the restored bluff and survey their opionions of their experiences.
1739.direct_services: The improved bluff will present an ideal venue for artists and photographers to work. The applicant will encourage local groups interested in drawing and painting to consider visting the restored bluff and using it as a subject for their art.
1739.outcome: The bluff erosion is so bad that it threatens the support structures to a nearby road, and the measure of success will be that this threat is mitigated. Trees have also fallen frequently due to the erosion. A professional engineer will examine the restored bluff and indicate the extent to which the roadway has been secured.

1233.description: The project will construct a resilient facility that can perform as fully functional post-disaster center and also as a reunification center in times of certain community emergencies. This enhancement would significantly bolster the City’s emergency response capabilities and ensure continuity of services when they are needed most. Also improving indoor space for logistics for an existing park designated as a POD in the City's and Broward DEM emergency plans. Funding will be used for the construction of a 44,000 SF new critical facility. Construction will consist of site preparation, exterior shell, interior build-out, emergency power, and support infrastructure. All funds, both state and local, will be for contractual services.
1233.purpose: The project will construct a resilient facility that can perform as fully functional post-disaster center and also as a reunification center in times of certain community emergencies. This enhancement would significantly bolster the City’s emergency response capabilities and ensure continuity of services when they are needed most. Also improving indoor space for logistics for an existing park designated as a POD in the City's and Broward DEM emergency plans.

Post-Disaster Operations: continuity of government (COG) functions, enabling essential services to continue after hurricanes or other disasters, logistics hub for resource management, stag

Reception and triage of affected families; Private meeting rooms for notifications; Mental-health and victim-support services; increase community access to critical services during recovery periods. Provide indoor storage for Water, food, tarps, ice, and
1233.population: The project will benefit the entire community with a critical facility that provides a post-disaster recovery center, including continued governmental operation. The City will use the facility directly after an event to provide information and services such as recovery schedules, public assistance, food and water distribution, and charging stations.
1233.outcome: The benefits of the project can be measured in the short term by the ability of the City to incorporate the new facility into its emergency management response plans. In the long term, the benefits would be from the use of the facility to provide post-disaster recovery services to residents of the community after a disaster such as a hurricane or mass shooting event.

2244.description: To combat the alarming global rise of antisemitism, the Hate Ends Now traveling cattle car and original artifact collection will visit schools across Florida. Students will experience an immersive presentation in a replica Holocaust-era cattle car, hear survivor testimonies, view authentic artifacts, and engage in guided discussion. This project aims to increase students' knowledge of the Holocaust in alignment with legislation such as Florida Statute 1003.42 (g) 1., inspire action against antisemitism and hate, and prepare them for post-secondary educational and work experiences by fostering the skills to engage constructively with challenging topics.
2244.purpose: The goal is to raise awareness of antisemitism and all forms of hate through a thought-provoking Holocaust educational program that is brought directly to schools across the state of Florida. By aligning with the State's Holocaust education objectives, the program complements existing classroom instruction and inspires students to consider their role in building a more tolerant society. Funding will support staffing and operations necessary to deliver effective State-wide programming.
2244.activities: We will provide management and coordination for the traveling replica cattle car exhibit across Florida. This includes scheduling, logistics, and delivering the immersive educational program. The services encompass the multimedia presentation, access to historical artifacts, and docent-led discussions to teach the lessons of the Holocaust and combat hate.
2244.direct_services: The funding provides a replica cattle car exhibit that travels through the State and offers a 20-minute immersive multimedia presentation with survivor narratives and historical video projections. It includes interaction with historical artifacts and guided discussions led by trained docents to educate citizens (especially students) on the Holocaust, combating antisemitism and hate.
2244.population: The target population served by this project is grade school, high school and university students throughout Florida. Hate Ends Now anticipates that about 20,000 students will visit the traveling cattle car exhibit and artifact collection during the 2026-2027 school year.
2244.outcome: The Hate Ends Now Exhibit increases students' understanding of the Holocaust and its relevance today, while building empathy and strengthening their ability to recognize and reject hate in their lives and communities. After the program, history and social studies teachers use a follow-up curriculum and gather meaningful student feedback to assess impact and measurable learning outcomes.

2954.description: In light of failing septic systems and pollution issues into local waterways, the goal is improving water quality through innovative wastewater treatment solutions. Senate Bill 796, which focuses on distributed wastewater treatment systems (DWTS), is a potential solution for residents struggling with outdated septic systems that are too expensive to replace and hook into the community's public sewer utilities. This Pilot Program will establish an administrative process for replacing eligible septic systems and utilize funds to replace septic tanks until funds are exhausted.
2954.purpose: The goal of the Septic Pilot Program is to establish an administrative process for selecting eligible applicants and replace septic systems until funds are exhausted.
2954.activities: The Clay County Board of County Commissioners will establish an administrative process for selecting eligible properties for the program. Activities include: Screening applicants, procuring a 3rd party contractor, and completing final inspections.
2954.direct_services: Properties selected through the Septic Pilot Program will be eligible to receive a replacement septic system in areas where sewer is not available.
2954.population: County residents will have the opportunity to apply for the Septic Pilot Program. County staff will develop scoring criteria to select eligible projects based on need. The County's intent is to replace deficient septic systems until funds are exhausted. The average price of a new Septic system in Florida is estimated to cost between $10,000 - $15,000.
2954.outcome: It is expected that the project will improve physical health through cleaner, healthier water for the community and wildlife. This benefit will be measured by monitoring water quality in adjacent areas.

2970.organization: Clay County Board of County Commissioners
2970.description: The Clay County Public Safety Complex is designed to include a Multi-Agency Warehouse, Fleet Center, Administrative Building, 911 Call Center, and Training Complex all situated on a new campus. These combined facilities will allow for consolidation and greater coordination between the Clay County Sheriff's Office and Public Safety (Fire Rescue). The Administration Building is essential to serve as a center for staff coordination during natural disasters and other emergencies.
2970.purpose: The Public Safety Administration Building is essential to serve as a center for staff coordination during daily operations, natural disasters, and other emergencies.
2970.activities: Essential public safety services across the County for citizens. Improved Public Safety performance, operational efficiencies, and response.
2970.direct_services: Once constructed, the Public Safety Complex will serve as the nexus for coordinating all public safety activity in the County. These services include CCSO, Fire-Rescue, and coordinating various departments during emergencies and disaster declarations. The facility will be a regional resource center for the State, Camp Blanding, NAS JAX, and other partners.
2970.population: The general population of Clay County is the target population served by the proposed Clay County Public Safety Complex.
2970.outcome: Benefits include: Reduced Response times from both the Clay County Sheriff's Office and Clay County Public Safety. Expected Outcome/Methodology: Reduction in call times which are monitored by CCSO and Public Safety and tracked using UCR, NIBRS, and NFIRS.

Additionally, this project would fund improvements throughout the Courthouse building including renovating existing public restrooms to ensure ADA compliance, building plumbing repairs and improvements, and, elevator replacement.

1948.description: The LBSF Project is designed to bring awareness to the importance of physical and mental health while creating a safe space for children. After school, third to fifth graders will complete a warm up, stretching, drills, and an endurance building workout. Sessions will end with a cool down followed by a healthy snack to teach campers the importance of nutrition and hydration. Two days a week a mental health professional will facilitate yoga and teach social-emotional awareness to provide mental health balance. The other three days will be dedicated to physical fitness and nutrition.
1948.purpose: The Lyles Brothers Sports Foundation will empower youth through the awareness of physical and mental health by: 1. Providing direct services to 180 children to teach physical fitness, nutrition, and social-emotional skills with an overarching focus on mental health. 2. Collaborating with partner organizations to provide basic needs to children and families in need, via community outreach activities.
1948.activities: Two six 6 Week long After School programs in the fall of 2026 for 60 children Two six week long After School Programs in the Spring of 2026 for 60 children Two Summer Camps in the summer of 2026 for 60 Children
1948.direct_services: The LBSF after school clinics and summer camps focus on teaching the importance of physical fitness which decreases obesity and enhances mental health. Community activities will provide basic needs to families such as winter clothing/coats, school supplies.
1948.population: Grade school students, At-risk youth, economically disadvantage persons and victims of crimes. 180
1948.outcome: 1. Program participants will demonstrate improved physical fitness when given measures that assess individual flexibility, agility, strength, and speed. Participants will be assessed on the following measures at the beginning and end of each session; including but not limited to: A. One mile run time B. Pacer time C. Number of Push Ups D. Number of Pull Ups E. Timed Shuttle Run 2. Participants will demonstrate improved awareness of emotional regulation skills measured by completing a pre and post assessment.

3311.description: This request is for the purpose of providing assistance to Citrus County residents impacted by ongoing and future septic-to-sewer conversion projects. Under FDEP policy, grant funding from FDEP is limited to costs directly related to septic tank abandonment and physical sewer connection. The exclusion of connection fees has resulted in significantly higher out-of-pocket costs for Citrus County residents as new sewer connections become available in their area. If funded, this request would allow the County to implement a reimbursement program that would provide cost reimbursement for impact fees and and plumbing expenses.
3311.purpose: These funds will allow Citrus County to implement a cost reimbursement program for residents with a residential property impacted by ongoing and future septic-to-sewer conversion projects. This appropriation would provide critical support to residents transitioning to central sewer service in the near term, thereby further assisting in reducing nutrient loading in our impacted spring-sheds and decreasing the environmental impacts that can be caused by excess nutrient loading.
3311.activities: As a result of this funding, Citrus County will be able to implement a cost reimbursement program for residents that have been impacted by ongoing and future septic-to-sewer conversion projects. This service would encourage and further promote participation in septic-to-sewer conversions in impacted areas of the county.
3311.direct_services: The successful funding of this request would result in the implementation of a cost reimbursement program that can better assist residents in covering the out-of-pocket costs associated with a septic-to-sewer conversion on his or her property. Citrus County will review and process reimbursement requests for eligible properties. Furthermore, the county plans to create an annual summary that will re
3311.population: The target population directly serviced by this project would be residents with property impacted by ongoing and future septic-to-sewer conversion projects. This potentially impacts multiple areas around the county that have had centralized sewer systems implemented consistent with state law.
3311.outcome: Some of the expected benefits of this project would be enhancements to environmental preservation and wildlife quality, improvements to wastewater management, groundwater quality, and surface water quality, and overall reductions in out-of-pocket costs to benefited properties. This will come as a result of encouraging more residents to complete sewer conversions. Moreover, the County plans to create an annual summary of the total number of requests received from residents and the total reimbursement dollars distributed each fiscal year.

1168.description: The Sarasota Bradenton International Airport has grown over 300% from 1,300,000 to 4,500,000 passengers necessitating increases in public safety personnel. All dispatch services are handled in a communications facility in terminal which is not hurricane hardened. Airport lost over 100,000 sq ft of roof in last storm and water leaks endangered entire public safety communications. This project would provide a secure, hurricane hardened facility.
1168.purpose: The Sarasota Bradenton International Airport has grown over 300% from 1,300,000 to 4,500,000 passengers, thereby necessitating increases in public safety personnel. All dispatch services are handled in a communications facility in terminal which is not hurricane hardened. Airport lost over 100,000 sq ft of roof in last storm and water leaks endangered entire public safety communications. This project would provide a secure, hurricane hardened facility.
1168.activities: Construction of the facility only. All operational services will be funded by the airport.
1168.direct_services: Project would guarantee public safety communications for the entire airport even during the most severe hurricane conditions including Police, Fire and Emergency medical Services and response to mass casualty, active shooter, terrorism and weather emergencies.
1168.population: Over 10 million passengers and greeters use the airport each year and all would be served.
1168.outcome: Public Safety of all the users of the airport

1082.description: The Town of Ocean Ridge has developed a multi-year capitol improvement plan for the potable water systems. The goal is to replace end-of-life water mains throughout the system, improving the quality of water provided to residents, providing an increase in system-wide water pressure and ensuring the system has the necessary sustained volume and flow to provide required fire protection throughout the community. The project is to replace approximately 1,200 linear feet of 6 inch cast iron water main with a new 10 inch HDPE water main that will meet the current fire code requirements and drinking water standards.
1082.purpose: The funds will be used in addition to local funding to support the replacement of approximately 1,200 linear feet of aging 6-inch cast iron water main with modern 10-inch HDPE main. This will enhance the reliability of Ocean Ridge's potable water system, improve water pressure and flow, meet fire code requirements, and protect water quality for residents, businesses, and visitors.
1082.activities: The funds will be used to augment local funds paying for the construction of new potable water mains. As part of the Town's CIP, $2.9 million was spent in FY 2023-2024 on water main replacement, and in FY 2024-2025, $1.25 million was allocated for this phase.
1082.direct_services: The project will ensure consistent delivery of clean, safe drinking water and adequate water pressure for fire protection. It will reduce the risk of water contamination and enhance the resilience of the system to support daily needs and emergency response.
1082.population: The target population includes over 1,800 Ocean Ridge residents, in addition to year-round visitors of Oceanfront Park.
1082.outcome: Increased water flow. It will be measured by testing flow from existing hydrants and comparing to test result received prior to construction.

1249.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General
1249.description: The Legal Services Clinic is a stand-alone non-profit organization, 501 (c) 3, whose primary mission is to offer no-cost and/or affordable legal assistance to everyone that cannot afford legal representation. The Clinic's continuing mission is to provide legal services for underserved communities with legal needs, providing legal assistance to persons who are Pro Se but cannot understand or properly prepare the Pro Se forms in Orange, Osceola, and Seminole County. We have been providing that assistance for the last years. Critically important in Orange, Seminole and Osceola.
1249.purpose: Competent legal services to low-income families who otherwise would not have access to legal representation. Our Pro Se project assists citizens who cannot fill out the forms for actions such as divorces, name changes, child support, and paternity. This allows for more efficient administration of the court dockets, as the Judges look at well-prepared complaints and petitions, which reduces the time for the court to attempt to understand the basis of the complaint when drafted by non-professional
1249.activities: Any competent legal representation deemed necessary. The Pro Se service makes access to the courts available to thousands who cannot have access without assistance. This program also allows for more efficient administration of the court dockets as the Judges are looking at well-prepared complaints and petitions which reduces the time for the courts to attempt to understand the basis of the complaint when drafted by non-professionals.
1249.direct_services: Legal representation and guidance. Our attorneys and staff are all bilingual and can assist both the citizens and the clerks, who cannot give legal advice on how to prepare these forms. We are able to assist the citizens, the clerks of Orange, Seminole, and Osceola Counties, and the courts all at the same time. Effectively this expenditure is cost cost saving measure.
1249.population: Our primary mission is to offer no cost and/or affordable legal assistance to that are in need of legal representation that cannot afford it. We expect to serve as many as possible. The number of clients served will be based on available funding. We will provide assistance in family law cases, misdemeanors, power of attorneys, wills and testaments, and Chapter 7 bankruptcies.
1249.outcome: We have in the past provided clean deliverables in the number of cases and consultations that we can provide with funding available. We can expect to provide hundreds of legal consultations, which we can process.

1921.description: The Lake Willie Boardwalk Project will transform the existing structure into a modern, resilient, and secure pedestrian corridor. Through a comprehensive assessment and complete reconstruction, the project will enhance public safety, accessibility, and user experience. The new design incorporates weather-resistant composite decking, durable materials, and vandal-resistant features to ensure long-term reliability with emphasis on a family-friendly environment. Beyond infrastructure improvements, this renovation reflects a reinvestment in community pride, environmental stewardship, and the shared well-being of residents and visi
1921.purpose: The funds will be used to structurally repair Lake Willie Boardwalk for vital safety, accessibility, connectivity of pedestrians, and recreational access between Carver Park and Cardinal Cove, two major community recreation areas in our city. In addition to the repairs, security and mitigation for vandalism needs to be addressed to reduce infrastructure damage. When completed, the boardwalk will be adequately lit with solar lights and up-to-date security features. Structural improvements will mi
1921.activities: Carver Park is the City's largest park, offering basketball courts, BBQ and picnic tables, a variety of playground equipment, and a sports pavilion. Cardinal Cove compliments these offerings with tennis and pickle ball courts, paved walking/jogging trails, improved fishing access, and upcoming improvements for intercity youth water sports, including a kayak dock addition.
1921.direct_services: This project will provide residents of Cardinal Park and Carver Park communities with a safe and reliable pedestrian and cycling route by repairing and rehabilitating the Lake Willie boardwalk. It will directly enhance services for the public, particularly teenagers and adults, who use the boardwalk daily for commuting to school, work, recreational parks, neighboring communities, and local busines
1921.population: The target population served by the Lake Willie boardwalk project is approximately 4,917 disadvantaged residents and pedestrians from Carver Park and Cardinal Cove communities who reside within a 10-mile radius of Lake Willie. This includes the City of Eustis' Parks and Recreation enrolled students who regularly utilize this boardwalk for outdoor activities.
1921.outcome: The expected benefits of this project will be improved quality of life for residents, students and recreational users who regularly utilize the Lake Willie boardwalk. Enhancements will include increased safety, improved mobility, elevated aesthetic appeal, and support for the continued economic growth. We commit to a six-month progress/status report and/or completion within one year. When completed, residents of the Carver and Cardinal Park communities as well as the general public, students, and recreational users will have full access to utilize the renovated boardwalk.

2587.description: Mirage Lake is prone to flooding during high rainfall events such as hurricanes and tropical storms. A preliminary engineering study determined that installing a weir structure device will allow the lake to drain naturally into the LPGA canal system prior to a major storm event. This will increase its capacity to hold rainwater. Installing back-flow prevention devices will help retain water in the pond without backflow through the existing storm pipe system to residential areas which are lower than the top of the lake bank. This project was requested by local residents during City Commission public meetings.
2587.purpose: The stormwater improvements will reduce water levels in Lake Mirage during low tide periods prior to major rain events. This will create a greater capacity to mitigate local flooding.
2587.activities: The funding will be used to finalize the design, provide survey, permitting and construction of lake improvements and install backflow preventer devices to storm pipes entering the lake. This will stop floodwater from flowing back through existing stormwater structures into local neighborhoods.
2587.direct_services: Residents in local neighborhoods will experience less flooding during high rain events.
2587.population: There are approximately 120 homes surrounding Lake Mirage representing 240 residents who are directly affected by the flooding of the lake. More than 1,500 homes (3,000 residents) would indirectly benefit from increased stormwater storage which will reduce traffic hazards from road flooding.
2587.outcome: The local low tide levels at Lake Mirage will be lowered to create additional capacity to store stormwater in an environmentally safe and efficient manner.

1120.description: Funding will allow inSIGHT Through Education, Inc to bring the Hate Ends Now Cattle Car to approximately 10,000 students at 15 schools and colleges throughout Palm Beach County. This multi-sensory traveling Holocaust exhibit provides an immersive lesson about the history of the Holocaust (1933-1945) instilling empathy in students as they gain awareness of hatred and the harm it can cause. As incidents of antisemitism and hate surge in Palm Beach County and in the state of Florida, it is urgent to provide Holocaust education to students in keeping with Section 233.061 of the Florida Statutes (Chapter 94-14, Laws of Florida).
1120.purpose: The funds will allow inSIGHT Through Education, Inc to bring the Hate Ends Now Cattle Car to approximately 10,000 students at 15 high schools and colleges throughout Palm Beach County. This multi-sensory traveling Holocaust exhibit provides an immersive lesson about the history of the Holocaust (1933-1945) instilling empathy in students as they gain awareness of hatred and the harm it can cause.
1120.activities: Funding will be used to provide approximately 10,000 students at approximately 15 public high schools and colleges in Palm Beach County with the opportunity to experience the traveling Holocaust exhibit. The multi-sensory exhibit will reach approximately 1,300 Palm Beach County students per week during its 7 week tour.
1120.direct_services: Set inside a replica World War II cattle car, students will get a powerful look at the history of the Holocaust through a multi-sensory exhibit to learn testimonies of survivors as well as key events of the Holocaust through World War II artifacts with a trained educator.
1120.population: High school and/or college students in Palm Beach County will be served by this project. Approximately 10,000 students from 15 public high schools and/or colleges in Palm Beach County will have the opportunity to visit the traveling Holocaust exhibit. The multi-sensory exhibit will reach approximately 1,300 students in Palm Beach County per week during its 7 week tour.
1120.outcome: The expected outcome is that students will have increased empathy and the profound harm that hatred can cause. Attendees of the exhibit will be encouraged to complete an online survey to help measure the effectiveness of this program. Questions will gauge Holocaust knowledge levels before and after participation, the emotional impact of the exhibit on their level of empathy, and if the experience has influenced their willingness to stand up when others are mistreated or harmed. Surveys will be administered and tabulated to measure the benefits of this unique educational experience. Reports by participating teachers will also be reviewed to maximize program success.

3192.description: The City of Clewiston (City) is respectively requesting an appropriation of $1.8 million to fund the design, construction, and equipping of a three-story Volunteer Firefighter Training Tower in Clewiston, Florida. This facility will serve as a critical training ground for volunteer firefighters, providing safe, realistic, and NFPA-compliant environments to prepare for fire suppression, rescue operations, and emergency response. The facility will serve as a Regional Training Hub, ensuring that the Hendry and Glades County community volunteer firefighters are properly trained.
3192.purpose: Currently, no dedicated training tower exists in Hendry or Glades County; volunteers must travel long distances for live-fire or multi-story training, reducing training frequency and increasing costs. The training tower facilities ensure the community's volunteer firefighters are as properly trained as compared to career departments in larger counties.
3192.activities: The training facility will be utilized to train firefighting advanced skills such as: high-rise and multi-story fire suppression, search & rescue in smoke-filled environments, ventilation and ladder operations, confined space and rope rescue and incident command and firefighter survival drills.
3192.direct_services: Investment in this training tower will directly strengthen the safety and resilience of our community while honoring the service of our volunteer firefighters.
3192.population: The Clewiston Fire Department covers both the City of Clewiston and unincorporated Hendry County, responding to approximately 800 calls per year with a limited number of career personnel supported by volunteer firefighters.
3192.outcome: The project enhances volunteer firefighter readiness and improved firefighter skill and safety. Measurable decreased response times and reduced injuries and property loss will result. A Regional Training Hub will serve surrounding rural communities, lowering costs by eliminating travel to distant facilities.

3110.description: In order to construct an alternate route to US 98 (Panama City Beach Parkway) in Bay County, property within the Breakfast Point Mitigation Bank (BPMB) must be used for roadway right of way. The County is required to pay for credit loss from the BPMP. Bay County is requesting assistance with bank reimbursement.
3110.purpose: A new roadway will be constructed between North Clara Avenue and Chip Seal Parkway relieving traffic congestion along Panama City Beach Parkway.
3110.activities: Mitigation credits will be acquired from Breakfast Point Mitigation Bank for the loss of credits due to the County acquiring right of way for the proposed roadway.
3110.direct_services: Better traffic flow and increases in safety for the traveling public.
3110.population: Citizens and guest that travel US 98 west of Hathaway Bridge. Estimated average daily traffic during peak season is 60,000 vehicles per day.
3110.outcome: Reduced travel times and increases in traffic safety.

1950.description: The City of Bushnell is requesting funds to build a new Master Lift Station to replace aging infrastructure and resolve critical issues in its regional wastewater system. The current station is central to multiple feeder stations, accepts all of City of Webster's wastewater through an interlocal agreement, is over capacity, lacks functional emergency power, and suffers from structural and equipment deterioration, leading to frequent operational disruptions. Planned upgrades include a new wet well, modern pumps and electrical systems, SCADA integration, and floodproofing to improve resiliency, safeguard public health, and support growth across Sumter County. Bushnell is updating its interlocal agreement with Webster to expand treatment capacity from 175,000 g from Webster to 400,000 gallons per day, reinforcing the project’s regional importance.
1950.purpose: The specific purpose is to help Bushnell construct a new Master Lift Station that directly addresses critical infrastructure vulnerabilities and enhances regional wastewater resiliency. The funding will support the replacement of an aging, over-capacity station that currently lacks fixed emergency power and suffers from structural degradation and outdated equipment.
1950.activities: To meet the intended purpose of these funds, the City of Bushnell will construct a new Master Lift Station equipped with a modern wet well, upgraded pumps and valves, waterproofed electrical systems, and enhanced SCADA instrumentation for remote monitoring. These improvements will provide reliable emergency power, mitigate flood risks, and ensure stable wastewater service for the region’s interconnected lift stations.
1950.direct_services: Direct services will not be provided to the citizens of Bushnell.
1950.population: The target population served by the project is the residents of City of Bushnell, population 3,148, and the City of Webster, population 1,631, for a total population served of 4,779.
1950.outcome: The project will improve regional wastewater reliability by replacing the aging, over-capacity Master Lift Station with modern infrastructure, reducing flood risk, preventing system failures, and ensuring uninterrupted service for multiple feeder stations. The outcome of the project will be measured by tracking reductions in overflow incidents, analyzing SCADA system data for performance improvements, verifying compliance through discharge monitoring reports, and comparing emergency response costs before and after construction to assess financial ben

2546.description: The purpose of this grant is to address the recruitment and retention crisis in the Florida law enforcement community by reducing the likelihood of officers leaving the profession, increasing improved sleep, reduction in overall stress levels and an increase in officer wellbeing, recruiting higher quality candidates, developing higher quality candidates, developing new recruits and cadets, and harnessing full officer potential.
2546.purpose: The Florida Law Enforcement Recruitment and Retention Grant Program will be administered to help State Troopers and local agencies recruit, develop, and retain the next generation of law enforcement officers blending the best practices from the FBI National Academy, International Coaching Federation (ICF) into an unparalleled professional development program.
2546.activities: The purpose of this grant is to address the recruitment and retention crisis in the Florida law enforcement community by reducing the likelihood of officers leaving the profession, increasing improved sleep, reduction in overall stress levels, and an increase in officer wellbeing, recruiting higher quality candidates, developing new recruits and cadets, and harnessing full officer potential.
2546.direct_services: Industry exclusive training in the form of recruitment academy: audit, bootcamp, sightline lite, ART and leadership bootcamp teaching generational leadership.
2546.population: Hundreds of officers from the Florida Highway Patrol, local police departments, and Sheriff's office
2546.outcome: Aggregate Field Trial Status and Results: •70% Reduction in Intention to Quit •64% Reduction in Desire to Change Roles •69% Reduction in Desire to Switch Agency •65% Increase in Overall Life Happiness •51% Reduction in Daily Stress •42% Increase in Attitudes Toward Job •37% Increase in Attitudes Towards Colleagues •99% Would Recommend to a Peer in the Law Enforcement Community Can provide comprehensive recruitment / retention data from pilot programs across the country.

3348.description: The proposed infrastructure improvement project involves the replacement of a failing storm drain system along Avenue Q between 14th and 17th Streets in Fort Pierce, Florida. The scope includes the installation of approximately 1,200 linear feet of 48-inch storm drain pipe and eight new drainage structures to enhance storm-water management and mitigate flooding risks. In addition to the drainage upgrades, the project will include the replacement of deteriorated curb and gutter, Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) ramp enhancements, and full roadway resurfacing to improve safety, accessibility, and mobility. Frances K. Sweets Elementary School is located within the project boundary, making these improvements critical to ensuring a safer environment for students, pedestrians, and local residents. The project supports the city's broader goals of infrastructure resilience, public safety, a
3348.purpose: The funds requested through the Senate appropriations process will directly support the City of Fort Pierce’s goal of improving public safety, infrastructure resilience, and equitable access to transportation. Specifically, the project will: mitigate flooding risks, enhance pedestrian and vehicular safety, create a safer environment for students and families, support long-term infrastructure reliability, and advance the city’s strategic priorities for sustainable development and inclusive mobili
3348.activities: To meet the intended purpose of the requested funds, the City of Fort Pierce will carry out the following activities and services as part of the infrastructure improvement project: construction and infrastructure upgrades and community safety and accessibility enhancements.
3348.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide the following direct services: improved public safety and accessibility, school zone enhancements, and storm-water management services.
3348.population: The target population served by this project includes: students, staff, and families of Frances K. Sweet Elementary School, residents and pedestrians, and motorists and cyclists. Based on local demographic data and school enrollment figures, between 2,600 and 4,600 individuals will be served.
3348.outcome: The primary outcome of this project is to significantly improve public safety, stormwater management, and accessibility along Avenue Q between 14th and 17th Streets in Fort Pierce. Specifically, the project will: reduce flooding and storm water accumulation, enhance pedestrian and vehicular safety, create a safer environment for students and families, and extend the lifespan and reliability of public infrastructure. The success of the project will be measured using the following methods: pre- and post-construction, assessments, ADA compliance audits, Roadway condition surveys, Community feedback and school safety reports, and Maintenance and service call logs.

3639.description: As required by Chapter 2024-180, HB1557, and Ch. 403.086(1)(c)3, F.S, this project will upgrade stage 1 and stage 2 for the improvements to Cemetery Road Wastewater Treatment Facility to meet Advanced Wastewater Treatment (AWT) standards for total nitrogen (3 mg/L) and total phosphorus (1 mg/L). The facility provides reclaimed water for agricultural reuse. Funds will support facility planning, engineering, design, permitting, and phased construction including a new influent pump station, headworks and odor control, and refurbishment of oxidation ditch treatment units with nutrient removal capability. The project ensures regulatory compliance, protects water quality in Lake Okeechobee Watershed Basin (BMAP area), and supports sustainable agriculture.
3639.purpose: To address State mandate of Chapter 403.086(1)(c)3 Florida Statutes requires; By July 1, 2034, any wastewater treatment facility providing reclaimed water that will be used for commercial or residential irrigation or be otherwise land applied within a nutrient Basin Management Action Plan (BMAP) or reasonable assurance plan area must meet the advanced water treatment standards for total nitrogen and total phosphorus. Stage 1 & 2 to upgrade the Cemetery Road WWTF to meet AWT standards and obtain
3639.activities: To seek contractual services through the OUA's procurement policies and procedures to address Stage 1 & 2 of the project that includes facility planning, engineering, design, permitting, and construction of influent pump station, headworks and odor control and one of the two oxidation ditch treatment units and nutrient control/ treatment capability in this Rural Area of Opportunity formerly known as Rural Area of Economic Concern.
3639.direct_services: Provides environmentally compliant wastewater treatment, protects Lake Okeechobee Watershed & Estuary, and supplies nutrient-managed reclaimed water for agriculture. Meets state agency BMAP rules and regulations and Chapter 403.086(1)(c)3 Florida Statutes
3639.population: The State of Florida as the Cemetery Road WWTF is in the Lake Okeechobee BMAP service area and does land apply treated plant effluent by means of spray irrigation to several different parcels. The Lake Okeechobee BMAP dated June 2025, includes Okeechobee County and more specifically the Taylor Creek/Nubbin Slough area which is located in Rural Area of Opportunity (RAO) (s. 288.0656, Florida Statutes).
3639.outcome: To address State AWT mandate as per Chapter 403.086(1)(c)3 Florida Statute. project will protect drinking water supplies, improve surface and groundwater quality, and reduce nitrogen and phosphorus discharges into Lake Okeechobee. It will support agriculture with reclaimed water, safeguard public health, and strengthen environmental resilience. Success will be measured through effluent monitoring, compliance with AWT standards, and water quality reporting.

3689.description: To make additions to critical infrastructure in the historic University of Florida campus, including storm water, waste water, electric, heating, and telecommunications services to various facilities.
3689.purpose: To enhance campus infrastructure - This project will support the University's goal of providing a safe and sanitary campus for all students, employees and visitors while maintaining building code and accessibility compliance. Improved energy efficiency across facilities and critical infrastructure will reduce waste and save energy costs over time.
3689.activities: This project will support the University's goal of meeting the needs of a growing customer population of students, employees and visitors by enhancing, expanding, and supplementing the capacity of existing infrastructure on campus.
3689.direct_services: Will address needs of access and capacity by implementing a campus-wide infrastructure enhancement plan.
3689.population: The University's student population, employees and visitors to college facilities.
3689.outcome: Will address needs of access and capacity by implementing a campus-wide infrastructure enhancement plan. Building, campus and system reviews and customer surveys immediately following construction as well as through periodic access and capacity assessments will measure outcomes.

1473.description: This year, Big Bend Hospice Foundation, Inc. will contribute over $412,000 to help sustain programs that are not reimbursed by Medicare, Medicaid, or private insurance — including Charity Care, Bereavement Services, Music Therapy, Special Patient Needs, Valor Programs, and Spiritual Care. However, the true annual cost of these programs exceeds $800,000, leaving a funding gap of nearly $533,706. This request seeks to close that gap, ensuring that every patient and family in need—regardless of income or insurance status—receives the comfort, dignity, and compassion that define Big Bend Hospice.
1473.purpose: Big Bend Hospice requests $412,000 in mission support to sustain unfunded programs that serve our community with compassion and dignity. The Big Bend Hospice Foundation will contribute over $412,000 this year to support vital, non- reimbursed services including Charity Care, Bereavement, Music Therapy, Special Needs, Valor, Art Therapy, Therapeutic Touch, Virtual Reality Sessions, and Spiritual Care Programs.
1473.activities: The funds will be used for: Charity Care, Community Bereavement Service, Music Therapy, Special Patient Needs, Valor Program, Art Therapy, Therapeutic Touch, Virtual Reality Sessions, and Spiritual Care.
1473.direct_services: Provide hospice care regardless of ability to pay; offer free community bereavement support accross eight counties; deliver healing though music therapy; assist patients in crisis with meals, transport, and essentials; honor veterans through Valor ceremonies; and provide higher level of spiritual care for patients and families.
1473.population: In FY 2024, Big Bend Hospice served 2,497 patients and their families, including 16 patients who received full Charity Care at no cost (a total of $114,485 in uncompensated care). Yet demand for these services continues to grow, and the Foundation cannot meet the full financial burden alone.
1473.outcome: Independent studies confirm music therapy's efficacy in reducing pain, anxiety, and agitation while improving comfort and quality of life. All complementary therapies outcomes will be measured through patient records, number of visits, services supported, care plan reviews, and patient and family satisfaction surveys.

2144.description: The City of Port St. Lucie is seeking funding for one Class I Industrial injection well. The City of Port St. Lucie Utility Systems Department (USD) plans to construct the Rangeline Water Treatment Facility (RLWTF) by 2029. The RLWTF will utilize reverse osmosis (RO) as a treatment process. A deep injection well system is proposed to primarily be used for the disposal of RO concentrate and other non-hazardous RO water treatment by-products. The proposed injection well system will also be used to dispose of groundwater on occasions when there is a need to bypass the RLWTF with the groundwater supply.
2144.purpose: In order to meet population projections and demands on the potable water system, the City of Port St. Lucie must construct a new reverse osmosis (RO) water treatment facility by 2029. Per Florida Administrative Code (F.A.C.), the concentrate byproduct of the RO treatment process must be disposed of in an approved method so as to not adversely affect the environment. In order to meet these requirements, the city intends to drill two Class I deep injection wells, as approved by FDEP. The requested
2144.activities: The funds will be used to fund the construction portion of this project. Construction is to include drilling of the Class I deep injection well by a licensed water well driller to a depth of 3,350 ft., installation of casing pipe, and installation of pumps and all above ground appurtenances.
2144.direct_services: The Class I deep injection well is necessary to provide potable water to the residents of the City of Port St. Lucie and surrounding areas. Without means to properly dispose of concentrate, the new water treatment facility cannot produce potable water.
2144.population: This project will predominantly serve the southwestern portion of the city; however, this can also serve as assistance to the existing water treatment facilities in case of emergency. Approximately 100,000 residents can be served after the initial build out, with potential future expansion planned into the design and construction.
2144.outcome: The expected benefit would be the safe and effective disposal of concentrate, thus allowing for continued operation of the water treatment facility and production of reliable potable water. Water production and concentrate disposal are monitored and metered for reporting purposes.

3679.description: Wastewater Effluent disposal project to provide for treatment expansion. The project request is for the construction of a deep injection well, monitoring well and associated piping and pumping facilities. The project is designed and permitted and is necessary to provide for additional effluent disposal. Current effluent disposal occurs through sprayfield irrigation on a 1,000 acre leased facility. Additional treatment expansion cannot occur without additional effluent disposal capacity. Development pressure requires additional wastewater service. The County is under contract to design additional capacity but cannot do so without the deep injection well(s). The project will provide for public utility service and negate the installation of additional septic systems or private package plants throughout the County.
3679.purpose: Wastewater effluent disposal to provide for treatment expansion to meet demand, The funding is necessary to complete the project to fill the gap not covered by the wastewater capital charges. Provision of wastewater capacity will eliminate the installation of additional septic systems in the Peace River Basin and the watersheds that feed the Peace River. The Lower Peace River is a waterbody not meeting water quality standards and is the surface water supply for the Peace River Manasota Regional
3679.activities: Construction of Deep Injection Wells and associated monitoring wells and piping for effluent disposal. The wells are necessary as there is no additional acreage to expand the current effluent disposal srayfield.
3679.population: Unincorporated area of DeSoto County. The next expansion will serve approximately 3,000 more customers, commercial and residential.
3679.outcome: Availability of wastewater service. The outcome will be measured by the number of equivalent residential units of capacity that will be available and the ability of the County to expand the treatment component of the utility.

3029.description: This request is to revert and reappropriate $26,492,752 that has previously been funded to Gilchrist School District in the 24-25 and 25-26 legislative sessions. This money was allocated under the special facilities category for the construction of a new elementary school. Due to declining enrollment and other circumstances out of the districts control they no longer have the student enrollment, nor can they staff and maintain a new school, but existing facilities are in need of upgrades and maintenance.
3029.purpose: The funds will allow the district to make much needed repairs to existing facilities and to replace the existing fire and emergency systems in all the schools. The current systems are still working on windows 96 and can not be upgraded.
3029.activities: The funding will allow the district to provide the students with a safer more uninterrupted learning environment.
3029.direct_services: The funding will allow the district to provide the students with a safer more uninterrupted learning environment. The funding will also allow the district to provide a safer place for the citizens to hold the multiple public functions and programs that take place throughout the year.
3029.population: The students and citizens of the county are the target population. 20,000 or more people will be served.
3029.outcome: The outcome of this funding is a safer and less interrupted learning environment. School grades, student attendance, and student test scores are all ways this can be measured.

3688.description: The funds will be used to purchase a software as a service tool in order to better conduct investigations and queries of subjects engaged in criminal activity. The tool will be deployed to FDLE personnel throughout the state and across divisions. Aquiring this tool is expected to reduce man hours needed to complete analytical workups and the identification of criminal actors in a more efficient manner. The anticipated efficiencies should reduce backlogs and delays due to a finite amount of personnel in a ever evolving threat landscape.
3688.purpose: The funds will be used to purchase a software as a service tool in order to better conduct investigations and queries of subjects engaged in criminal activity. The tool will be deployed to FDLE personnel throughout the state and across divisions.
3688.activities: These funds will allow the purchase of an intelligence tool that will automate queries of disparate data sources and return results into one place. The current activities require users to conduct a multitude of queries to multiple data sources.
3688.direct_services: By leveraging this tool, the citizens of Florida will receive a more efficient method of identifying threats to the state, not only from a domestic security perspective, but also from those that commit crimes in the State. Furthermore, this tool will be leveraged to help quickly identify criminal illegal aliens and their associates that are in the State to enhance immigration law enforcement effor
3688.population: All Floridians and visitors are better served by a state that employs technological advances that make the state safter.
3688.outcome: Aquiring this tool is expected to reduce man hours needed to complete analytical workups and the identification of criminal actors in a more efficient manner. The anticipated efficiencies should reduce backlogs and delays due to a finite amount of personnel in a ever evolving threat landscape. A further benefit is cost-savings to the agency as some contracted services may no longer be needed due to this tool being able to conduct the same or similar business.

3708.organization: Historical Society of Palm Beach County
3708.description: Funds will support student field trips, educator-led lessons, interactive exhibits, and digital learning tools that connect Holocaust history to civic responsibility. Activities include guided discussions, reflection materials, transportation for Title I schools, and an updated exhibition highlighting local stories of courage and moral action.
3708.purpose: The funds will expand Holocaust and civic education through the Upstanders program, providing free field trips, digital learning tools, and a redesigned exhibition that connects global lessons of courage to Palm Beach County’s local history—empowering 3,000–4,000 students annually, especially from Title I schools, to practice empathy, moral responsibility, and community engagement.
3708.activities: Funds will support student field trips, educator-led lessons, interactive exhibits, and digital learning tools that connect Holocaust history to civic responsibility. Activities include guided discussions, reflection materials, transportation for Title I schools, and an updated exhibition highlighting local stories of courage and moral action.
3708.direct_services: The program will provide free, standards-based Holocaust and civic education to Palm Beach County students through interactive field trips, guided learning sessions, and digital access. It will remove transportation barriers for Title I schools and empower youth to practice empathy, responsibility, and community engagement.
3708.population: Economically disadvantaged persons; At-risk youth; Grade school students; High school students; University/college students
3708.outcome: The program will enrich cultural experience and improve quality of education by reaching 3,000– 4,000 students annually—at least half from Title I schools—who will demonstrate measurable growth in empathy, tolerance, and civic awareness through structured learning assessments and educator evaluations. Impact will be measured through pre- and post-visit surveys, teacher feedback forms, and student reflection exercises assessing changes in understanding of Holocaust history, empathy, and civic responsibility. Attendance data and digital engagement metrics will further track program reach and effectiveness.

3762.organization: New Life Men's and Women's Program, Inc
3762.description: NLDC currently provides residential substance abuse treatment to both male and female students on a single campus, an arrangement that is not ideal. To better meet programmatic and safety needs, NLDC plans to separate services by gender. The existing campus will be dedicated to female students, as its configuration is well suited for that purpose. NLDC seeks appropriated funding to purchase land and facilities for a new campus to serve male students, allowing for more appropriate treatment environments and improved outcomes for all participants.
3762.purpose: NLDC currently serves persons with substance abuse addictions on one campus for both male and female "students," which is not ideal. We thus intend to use the current campus for our female students, which is more appropriate due to its configuration, and desire to purchase new land and facilities for our male students.
3762.activities: As this is a capital outlay request, these funds will not be used directly for services, however all funds to NLTC serve the underlying purpose of improving the lives of those affected by severe drug and alcohol dependency addictions.
3762.direct_services: The purpose of the funds, if approved by the Legislature, would be for the purchase of new facilities to house male students of NLTC, and for them to receive the necessary addiction treatments services provided by NLTC.
3762.population: The target population served by this project include: homeless, drug users (in health services), and drug offenders (in criminal justice). The expected amount of individuals served is between 50 and 100.
3762.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is to reduce substance abuse. NLTC is a 43 year old organization with tremendous success in the treatment of those who suffer from substance abuse addictions, through a wholistic approach to wellness. This includes residential housing for one year, therapy, self awareness, and spiritual development. We change people's lives, and most remain drug and alcohol free for life. We recommend measuring by Five and ten year measurements for recidivism.

1680.description: The project involves the reconstruction of the SW 8th Avenue roadway, including surveying, removal, and replacement of the asphalt layer. The work requires removal, re-compaction, and grading of the base gravel course and sub-base before laying a new asphalt layer. Additional construction activities include installing utilities, grading, pavement base, curbs and gutters, concrete sidewalks, and landscape restoration to ensure a safe, durable, and visually enhanced roadway.
1680.purpose: The funding request supports the continuation of the Both Phases of the NW/SW 8th Avenue roadway projects. Work to be performed requires the survey, removal, and replacement of the asphalt course. Removal and re-compaction, grading of base gravel coarse and sub-base is necessary prior to replacement of the asphalt layer. New construction consists of but is not limited to: utilities, grading, pavement base, curb and gutter, asphalt pavement, concrete sidewalks and landscape restoration.
1680.activities: The services will support the reconstruction of SW 8th Avenue to create a safer, more efficient, and functionally improved environment. The project involves surveying, removing, and replacing the asphalt course, as well as re- compacting and grading the base gravel and sub-base to ensure a stable foundation. New utilities, grading, pavement base, curbs, gutters, asphalt pavement, concrete sidewalks, and landscape restoration will be installed to enhance road durability, pedestrian safety, and ov
1680.direct_services: The direct services provided to citizens by the appropriation project include enhanced safety for both motorists and pedestrians. Upgrading the roadway will reduce the risk of accidents and injuries by improving road conditions, adding new curbs and gutters, constructing safe pedestrian sidewalks, and ensuring smoother traffic flow. These improvements will make the area safer and more accessible f
1680.population: The target population served by this project includes economically disadvantaged individuals and the general population in the area surrounding SW 8th Avenue. The project is expected to benefit thousands of residents, commuters, and pedestrians who use this road daily, improving safety, traffic flow, and accessibility for all.
1680.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is improved safety for both motorists and pedestrians on SW 8th Avenue, which is a heavily utilized north-south street in Hallandale Beach. The planned enhancements, including roadway upgrades, new sidewalks, and traffic calming measures, will improve multi-modal conditions and reduce traffic speeds, making the area safer for pedestrians. The outcome will be measured by monitoring daily traffic counts to assess the impact on traffic flow and safety.

2426.description: The funds requested for the Cape Coral Water, Sewer & Irrigation Expansion Program will address critically low groundwater levels in the mid-Hawthorne aquifer and failing residential wells, a problem highlighted by the South Florida Water Management District water shortage order, by replacing outdated wells and septic tanks with reliable municipal water, sewer, and irrigation systems—protecting both public health and the environment, preventing aquifer depletion and water contamination, and supporting sustainable growth.

2426.activities: Any state funding awarded for the Cape Coral Water, Sewer & Irrigation Expansion Program will directly benefit property owners in northern Cape Coral by reducing the amount they are assessed (about $33,000) to pay for new utility connections. State appropriations received by the City are applied to offset the total project cost, resulting in a lower special assessment for each affected parcel.
2426.direct_services: State funding for the Cape Coral Water, Sewer & Irrigation Expansion Program will provide citizens with direct access to reliable municipal water, sewer, and irrigation services by enabling the installation of modern utility infrastructure across northeast Cape Coral, replacing aging wells and septic tanks to improve public health, environmental quality, and overall quality of life for local prope
2426.population: The Water, Sewer & Irrigation Expansion Program will serve about 3,100 properties within the city.
2426.outcome: The project improves environmental conditions by replacing septic tanks and shallow wells with municipal water and sewer systems, which protects aquifers from depletion and pollution, reduces risks to canals and groundwater, and promotes water conservation through reuse technology. Additionally, potable water services protect the mid- Hawthorn's aquifer water levels which have reached historic lows resulting in Water Management District water shortage.
